sutra.meaning: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga

sections.practice: attempt to take up one new practice or change in lifestyle in accordance with yamas and niyamas

sutra.sanskrit:
त॒तः॒ क्षी॒य॒ते प्रकाशा॑वर॒णम् 
धा॒र॒णासु च योग्यता॑ मन॒सः
sutra.meaning: From that is dissipated, the mental darkness which veils the light, ... and from that, is attained the state of the mind for linking the attention to a higher concentration force or person.

sections.insight: Pranayama removes the veil covering the light of knowledge and heralds the dawn of wisdom. The mind becomes fit, thereafter, for Dharana or concentration.. the next limb of yoga.Once the mind is still and free of thought it can focus on a single point. This is when it can manifest what it wants.
sections.practice: Make a commitment and effort to intensify your practice. Meditate for 20 min

sutra.meaning: The yogi must be so familiar with the realm of mind and emotions, that he should begin to recognize where thoughts, ideas, images and memories arise. Their particular location in the mind environment and emotional atmosphere should be known. Then he may practice the sixth stage of yoga, which is linking of the attention to a concentration force or person through a restricted location in the mento-emotional space.

sections.wisdomFrom: God is Omniscient, the most ancient One, the Controller, subtler than the subtlest, the Support of all, and the possessor of an inconceivable divine form; He is brighter than the sun, and beyond all darkness of ignorance. One who at the time of death, with unmoving mind attained by the practice of Yog, fixes the prāṇ (life-airs) between the eyebrows, and steadily remembers the Divine Lord with great devotion, certainly attains Him.
